background.text: Homelessness, you've been real vocal about homeless issues, particularly in this region and in this area. What is your assessment of how the city and the state have responded to some of these issues with people experiencing homelessness?

background.speaker: [target]
background.text: Well, first of all, this is coming off the Thanksgiving weekend, heading into the Christmas holidays. We want to make sure that anybody who doesn't have a home has a chance to have a home. I think you best do that by getting the prices of housing down, make housing affordable. But make sure that we've got the kinds of places set up where people can go help people. We've got so many generous people in this region who want to help those in need. Free that up. Let that happen. But creating tent cities harms the city, harms those involved. And I don't think there's many people in the city who believe it's a good idea other than the city council. background.text: You know, we've seen some IRS data that's indicating that Americans have cut charitable deductions by like several billion dollars. ground_truth: I haven't studied the current state of charitable giving and where it stands historically. I know I did some research on this when I was in school about looking at charitable giving over time. And what you see is a strong correlation to people of faith who tithe and give a standard amount of giving over time. And I think what you see is, you know, we saw about $100 million being donated by I think Bezos the last week. You see a decent amount of charity that's flowing in the state of Texas on a regular basis in the wake of Hurricane Harvey and so forth. Mattress Mac opened up his stores and let people sleep in his rooms. I think if you want to see charitable giving go up, stop putting so many demands and constraints on the American people. Free them up to do what they do best. Create jobs, create opportunity, and use their hearts and their dollars to go help others.
